cohort: The study included 28 mothers of early-preterm infants, 29 mothers of late-preterm infants, and 28 mothers of full-term infants in Malawi.
finding: Mothers of early-preterm infants reported significantly more distress symptoms than mothers of full-term infants, while distress scores for mothers of late-preterm infants fell between the other two groups.
mod_finding: Caesarean birth was associated with more distress symptoms, while the presence of a support person was associated with fewer symptoms.
gest_age: Early preterm, late preterm, and full-term
